chunks: From him, from Safwan and Fadalah, from al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the Imams (peace be upon them both): Regarding

a man who buys goods all together for a price, then values each garment at what it is worth until it amounts to his principal capital; does he sell it by Murabahah (cost-plus) one garment at a time? He (peace be upon him) said, 'No, until he makes clear to him that he only valued it [for the purpose of selling at that value].' I asked him about a man who buys goods all together; does he sell it by Murabahah one garment at a time? He said, 'No, until he makes clear to him that he only valued it [for that purpose].'
ai.seo_question: What is the condition for validly selling bulk goods individually at a profit in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the permissibility of *Murabahah* (cost-plus sale) for bulk goods, emphasizing that the seller must explicitly disclose that individual item prices are based on independent valuation rather than a strict proportional split of the original bulk cost. This distinction prevents *gharar* (ambiguity) and ensures the buyer understands the basis of the markup, a key principle in Shia commercial jurisprudence. The ruling underscores the importance of transparency in pricing structures to maintain the validity of the contract.
